content: DTNA dystrobrevin alpha is a protein in humans encoded by the DTNA gene. The protein encoded by the DTNA gene is a member of the dystrobrevin subfamily, which is part of the larger dystrophin protein family. This protein is an integral component of the dystrophin-associated protein complex (DPC). The DPC is composed of dystrophin and several other integral and peripheral membrane proteins, including dystroglycans, sarcoglycans, syntrophins, and both alphaand beta-dystrobrevin. The DPC is localized to the sarcolemma, the membrane surrounding muscle cells. Disruption of this complex is linked to various forms of muscular dystrophy, a group of genetic disorders characterized by progressive muscle weakness and degeneration. DTNA dystrobrevin alpha may play a role in the formation and stabilization of synapses, which are the junctions between nerve cells, as well as in the clustering of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, which are critical for neuromuscular signaling. Multiple alternatively spliced transcript variants of the DTNA gene have been identified, which encode different isoforms of the protein. Mutations in the DTNA gene have been associated with Meniere's disease, a disorder of the inner ear that can cause vertigo, hearing loss, and tinnitus. DTNA has been shown to interact with dystrophin, a key structural protein in muscle cells that is essential for maintaining the integrity of the muscle cell membrane.
